title: City Park sample screen (screen 6, the old oak)
note: Your picks of 26 Oct: the trees Pepper climbs at true width with one leaf mass whose top is above the world (decision 1), and young 6 m mid trees (decision 2b). Screen 6 at both cameras: up on the high road she runs through the old oak's leaves; down on the path the oak stands at full size with its branches as her ledges. New: the old oak (trunk 54 px), a park lime at x 1528 and an ash at x 1916 whose crown leans over the treetop walk, so screen 7's walk is in leaves too; three young mid trees (a lime, a maple, a birch, 139 px). After four review rounds (the oak re-cut from its own render with the lime's pipeline): no ink edges, no tree lighter than the tree line behind it, no loose limbs or flat crown cuts, clumps of 3 to 4 shades, old small crowns end cleanly beside the new ones. Nothing she stands on moved. Checks: PEPPER UNCHANGED, flow 125/125, Tiled, physics 97/97, QA 0 problems, curve T1-T4 PASS. Layers light to dark: sky 202, far city 191, tree line 181, mid 154-159, back 118-141, play 80-91. SpriteCook 284 credits.
question: Scale calls for you. Oak: trunk 54 px (1.2 m); the plan said 46 for the old oak and 60 for the big oak on screen 9. Lime and ash: trunks 36 and 29-33 px against the spec's 23 (0.5 m); both models drew them wider, and they sit inside the plan's true range for park trees (0.4 to 0.8 m). The lime's crown is now 371 px (8 m, the plan's lime crown). Keep these trunks, or ask for slimmer ones?
